environment.build: Rust dev/test, local Qt 6.11.2, offline workspace checks
environment.native_test: Qt Quick/WebEngine offscreen software fixtures; native_insert CTest 1/1
environment.performance: Offscreen software renderer; viewport 640x480 at 100% zoom; benchmark also ran 80% and 125%; devicePixelRatio reported by WebEngine
environment.wayland: No physical Wayland keyboard journey was run
environment.scope: Site-scoped selector discovery and action safeguards are implemented and fixture-tested. The real composed BrowserUi config lifecycle and comparable before/after performance remain unqualified.

baseline_comparison.result: Current-build renderer samples and a bounded expensive-selector stress measurement were recorded. There is no same-build pre-S12 baseline; the full T043 transfer/Rust-label/QML-overlay/action comparison was not performed. Initial test and lint failures are retained in their named logs and were fixed before the final passing runs.

observations: Workspace engine tests passed (426 tests); bounded hint payload parsing and privacy contracts remained green.
The production WebEngine fixtures passed T009 control-value privacy and literal label checks.
All 55 config tests passed, including selector layering, per-entry and resolved limits, site order, site-rule aggregate bytes, and empty replacement.
The full workspace check passed; engine unit tests covered the BrowserUi snapshot revision binding, and existing selector callback/parser unit contracts remained green.
The browser-owned WebEngine document accepted valid CSS and rejected malformed CSS through the existing selector syntax validation tests.

Global/profile/runtime and matching-site layers preserve stable extend/replace order; authored entries cap at 16 selectors while a resolved family allows 32; site rules share a 16 KiB selector-string budget.
Custom discovery and empty replace behavior passed for all, scrollables, and proxy candidate families; the default all policy remained independent.

A custom-selected semantic button survived fresh and final click checks. A revision mismatch rejected freshness. A generic custom match with a fake href remained aria-only and failed click, focus, and native-pointer preflight.
The 32-selector stress case inspected exactly 50,000 nodes, returned 5,000 candidates, set truncated=true, and passed the production WebEngine fixture.
One renderer pass using 32 selectors (31 relational :has selectors) took 772 ms at 50,000 inspected nodes and 5,000 output candidates; this is a single stress observation, not a p95.
The full workspace check passed, including the Rust workspace test suites and doctests.
All 126 QML/WebEngine tests passed, including the existing hint, rapid, proxy, geometry, and recovery regressions.
The native_insert CTest target passed 1/1 under the offscreen Qt test environment.
Generated-contract, architecture, release artifact, license, QML lint, formatting, workspace tests, and doctests passed.
Generated configuration documentation from the xtask source; the selector policy text is in the generator and matches the generated output.
Rust formatting passed.
Strict workspace Clippy passed with warnings denied.
Pack structure and its 24 contracts, 26 invariants, 57 planned tests, 28 slices, and 55 source items validated.

The renderer harness recorded 10 warm-ups and 100 samples for 500 candidates at 80%, 100%, and 125%, plus 1,000, 5,000, and 1,000-with-mutation cases. Current-build collection p95 values were 61.6, 54.2, 57.2, 112.6, 1066.4, and 108.3 ms respectively; fresh p95 values were 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.6, 3.7, and 0.7 ms.
T043 is not qualified as a comparable performance pass: no same-build pre-S12 baseline or full transfer/Rust-label/QML-overlay/action stage timings were collected.
test_results.reason: Current-build renderer samples exist, but the required before/after comparison and full interaction-stage measurements are absent; see the measurement limitations in performance-summary.json.

observations: Pack integrity and evidence/progress schema validation passed for the recorded S12 evidence.

remaining_risks: No composed offscreen BrowserUi journey exercises startup policy validation, matching-site resolution, commit/cancellation, stale callback handling, and final action through the complete configuration/session lifecycle.
The renderer benchmark is current-build evidence only. It omits Qt-to-Rust transfer, Rust labeling, QML overlay presentation, and final action delivery, and has no comparable pre-S12 sample set.
A synchronous CSS selector match cannot be interrupted. The traversal and candidate caps expose truncation, but a sufficiently expensive selector can still block the renderer during one match.
All Qt/WebEngine and native CTest evidence is offscreen; no physical Wayland keyboard qualification was performed.
not_run_reasons: T043 comparable performance qualification: current renderer samples exist, but no same-build pre-S12 baseline or full end-to-end stage timings exist.
Composed BrowserUi selector lifecycle: no offscreen integration fixture drives startup, site rules, config commit/cancel, stale callbacks, and final activation as one journey.
Physical Wayland keyboard journey: not run; offscreen Qt tests do not establish physical desktop interaction.
